children: Elon Musk is putting a deadline on one of AI's most disruptive cybersecurity risks, predicting that artificial intelligence will outperform human security experts at hacking by
late 2027

. The warning matters for investors because increasingly capable autonomous attack systems could accelerate spending on cybersecurity software, while raising risks for companies that fail to automate their defenses quickly enough.

Musk expects AI to reach superhuman performance across digital tasks, with hacking among the first major capabilities to cross that threshold. His forecast effectively gives corporate security teams roughly
16 months
to prepare for systems that could discover and exploit vulnerabilities faster than human attackers.
Recent developments suggest that shift is already beginning.
Software company JFrog
recently patched a critical vulnerability in its Artifactory software repository platform that carried a
9.8 out of 10 severity score

. The flaw could reportedly be exploited without authentication, creating potentially significant supply-chain risk because compromised software repositories can distribute malicious code across large numbers of customers.
AI systems are also increasingly being used to find vulnerabilities rather than merely defend against them. OpenAI model testing identified
nine separate zero-day flaws
in Artifactory during July evaluations.

Other technology executives are issuing similar warnings. Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch has argued that companies should prepare for software vulnerabilities to face autonomous attacks, while CTO Malte Ubl tested an open-weight AI model capable of independently writing code to search for bugs. Coinbase
CEO Brian Armstrong has separately predicted a major rogue-AI security event within two years.
Investor Takeaway
For investors, Musk's timeline could strengthen the long-term case for cybersecurity companies capable of automating threat detection, vulnerability discovery and incident response.
The key question is whether corporate cybersecurity budgets begin shifting faster toward
AI-driven defensive tools
as offensive capabilities improve.

Investors should watch customer spending trends, adoption of autonomous security products and whether vulnerability discoveries accelerate across widely used software infrastructure. A major AI-enabled cyberattack could sharply increase demand across the sector, while companies unable to defend increasingly automated software environments could face higher operational, regulatory and reputational risks.

title: Elon Musk Makes Startling AI Prediction
